aboutForumBlurb: The Information Systems Academics and Practitioners' Forum (ISAP Forum) is an independent, collegiate platform established at the University of Professional Studies, Accra (UPSA). Designed to bridge the historical divide between academic research and industry execution, ISAP brings together scholars, industry practitioners, policy architects, and students to examine national digital transformations and accelerate sustainable socioeconomic development.

introText: The Information Systems Academics and Practitioners' Forum (ISAP Forum) was established as a high-impact intellectual platform in Ghana and the broader West African sub-region. Headquartered at the University of Professional Studies, Accra (UPSA), the Forum provides an evidence-based, collaborative arena where academic insights directly interrogate and inform major enterprise architectures, digital public infrastructure, and national digital policies.
mission: To foster sustained, high-level interaction between Information Systems researchers and practicing technology professionals, translating scholarly investigation into real-world socioeconomic outcomes.
vision: To be the benchmark African platform for Information Systems thought leadership, fostering resilient, ethical, and inclusive socioeconomic development through digital systems.

bannerSubtitle: Public Sector Identification Systems for Socioeconomic Development: The Ghana Experience and Way Forward
aboutTheForum: The 2026 edition of the ISAP Forum focuses squarely on one of Africa’s most consequential governance and technology undertakings: the establishment and nationwide integration of Public Sector Identification Systems.

Over the past decade, Ghana has invested substantially in the National Identification System (the Ghana Card), managed by the National Identification Authority (NIA). The digital identity ecosystem has expanded rapidly from a foundational civil register into the mandatory verification layer for financial transactions, telecommunications SIM card registration, social security harmonization, tax administration, and public health delivery.

While the engineering and administrative progress of the rollout is undeniable, critical questions remain for Information Systems researchers and practitioners: What are the measurable impacts on financial inclusion and public revenue mobilization? How resilient is the underlying cryptographic and biometric infrastructure against data breaches and cyber threats? How can interoperability between disparate public and private registries be optimized without compromising citizen privacy and data sovereignty?
themeContext: Public Sector Identification Systems for Socioeconomic Development: The Ghana Experience and Way Forward

objectives.title: Empirical Assessment of Identity Platforms
objectives.description: Evaluate the actual economic, administrative, and technological performance of Ghana’s National Identification System.

objectives.title: Privacy, Ethics, and Data Sovereignty
objectives.description: Examine constitutional rights, biometric protection, data protection compliance, and ethical considerations surrounding mandatory state ID registries.

objectives.title: System Interoperability & Integration Architecture
objectives.description: Explore technical API protocols, cross-agency synchronization (GRA, SSNIT, NHIS, BoG), and public-private integration friction.

objectives.title: Financial Inclusion and Digital Economy
objectives.description: Analyze how biometric e-KYC has reshaped mobile money adoption, banking compliance, and credit bureau scoring across Ghana.

objectives.title: Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Resilience
objectives.description: Address disaster recovery, zero-trust architectures, biometric spoofing threats, and continuity protocols for mission-critical national data repositories.

objectives.title: Socioeconomic Inclusivity & Marginalized Groups
objectives.description: Interrogate access barriers for rural citizens, elderly demographics, and informal workers to ensure identity systems do not amplify exclusion.

objectives.title: National Policy Communiqué Formulation
objectives.description: Formulate an actionable, evidence-based policy communiqué for submission to the Ministry of Communications and Digitalisation, Parliament, and industry bodies.
